basis: Items 0-2: price is pinned by the fixed US$5.214 DNO cash offer; the interim cannot move it and every live catalyst sits outside the window.
against: A surprise Genel counter-bid or deal-break headline on the day, neither of which is dated inside the window.

basis: Item 0: the 1.4475p dividend (1.92% of spot) goes ex on the print day, the window is measured on unadjusted closes, and 8 of 10 prior ex-dates closed down a median 1.58%.
against: A clearly strong H1 or NAV uplift lifts the stock more than the dividend takes off, as on the 2025-03 and 2025-09 ex-dates.

basis: Item 0: the company guides conservatively by method, so the first FY27 EBITDA guide is likely well under the EUR 266m single-source consensus.
against: A conservative guide is the expected pattern and the stock already trades at a deep discount to that consensus; last year's low guide closed +1.46%, and a dividend reinstatement (item 1) could lift it.

basis: Item 0: consensus implies H2 revenue down about 2% YoY against July +23.9% and the collapse of the largest competitor (Headlam), and this is the first statement since; upgrade-style updates on this name have moved +4 to +12%.
against: The Headlam news is partly in the price after the 1 Sep jump, and H1 profit conversion (item 1) could disappoint as it did in Nov-25 (-12.5%).

basis: Items 0-1: H1 production of 43.7 kboepd is already above the 34-42 range, and Brent points to a production and FCF guide raise.
against: Peers and Brent make the arithmetic public, the last FCF upgrade was sold (-6.7%), Brent fell 7% just before the window, and debt and M&A concerns dominate this name.

basis: Item 0: BizLink, CRDO's sole AEC manufacturer, posted roughly +31% revenue growth from May to July against a guide implying 6-9% sequential, backed by the APH, FN and MRVL datacom prints.
against: The buy-side whisper for an AI darling is already above guide, the Q2 guide is pre-committed to mid-single digits (item 2) and may read as deceleration, and no pre-announcement this time (item 1).

basis: Items 0-1: third-shift hiring at Torrington and a new director's open-market buy, set against item 2 (out-of-the-money Fit warrants and no project trail).
against: Job postings are a proxy inference; FCEL prints are dominated by revenue misses and dilution, and the skew and downtrend reflect real doubt.

basis: Items 0-1: the first FY27 EPS guide must absorb about 9% more shares, management has cut EPS on deal costs before (-6.8%), and upside is bid on a rumour that confirmed deals have historically sold off.
against: The street has already modelled the CyberArk share count, and a strong NGS ARR or FY27 revenue guide can dominate; the rumour pop was already unwinding before the print.

basis: Item 0 (seat-priced AI Studio tiers ahead of first AI quantification) and item 2 (monday.com retention read).
against: A +16% run-up on short covering with the stock above the average target leaves a high bar, and the finance-leadership churn (item 3) adds guide risk.

basis: Items 0-1: Hormuz logistics costs worsened through the quarter against a guide that assumed easing, and leverage is near a tightened 3.25x covenant; 5 of 7 prior prints fell.
against: The stock is already -10% over 20 days on one estimate, and JELD-WEN's guidance raise shows the demand side may surprise.

basis: Item 0 (record US storage installs backing the ATS ramp) and item 3 (no insurance-reserve hit expected in Q3).
against: Read-throughs land with a lag on a labour-services name; three of the last four reactions were large negatives on margin and guide issues.

basis: Items 0, 1 and 4: an implied steep Q4 decline, a harvest strategy on the core business, and an unused shelf after a super-voting bump.
against: The event date is unconfirmed (cadence implausible), the guide was already public, and this is a micro-float name that can spike on anything.

basis: Item 0: the actual back-half tariff rate (~11%) is below the 15% baked into guidance, giving a likely guide raise beyond the refund.
against: The market discounts refund-flattered beats (Kohl's, Target per item 1); peer comps are weak and a new CFO may rebase the back-half guide.

basis: Items 0-2: week-adjusted growth is stronger than the headline, and the guide was set late in the quarter so the outcome distribution is narrow.
against: The refund is known, the La-Z-Boy read-through is soft (item 3), and the stock has fallen on 6 of 7 prints.

basis: Items 0 and 2-3: no reportable acquisition bridges the H2 guide, a promotional run-in rests on a product launch, and a 10% holder keeps selling.
against: Insiders bought at $3.25 (item 4) and a going-concern removal could lift the stock; the event date and cadence are weakly established.

basis: Items 1-2: the FY27 high-single-digit growth target is arithmetically stretched and MSA flagged slow AFG-funded fire-service orders.
against: The deferred divestiture gain (item 0) may produce a headline EPS beat, and the stock is already down about 7%; the baseline is thin.

basis: Item 0: IFC's fresh 144 sale programme restarts in print week at about 10x ADV, plus item 1 (the profitability claim rides on a Q4 with an impairment test).
against: A first three-year outlook (item 2) could signal confidence, and the 144 seller works over weeks rather than on one session.

basis: Items 0 and 13 (two independent hunts agree): the flat sequential guide contradicts last year's +9-10% Q2 seasonality, and airfare CPI stepped up about 12pp inside the quarter (items 1 and 12).
against: Corporate negotiated fares rise far less than retail CPI, the take rate may compress, and a conservative next-quarter guide could overwhelm the beat.

basis: Item 0: the two-analyst consensus has Q2 EPS falling while peer Teekay's audited Q2 spot TCE rose sharply, and TEN's own sensitivity implies a 30-50% beat; Q3-to-date rates are at records (item 3).
against: Tanker investors trade the rate tape rather than stale consensus, so a +14% run-up near the 52-week high may already hold the beat; Q2-Q3 drydocks (item 1) and no dividend (item 2) could disappoint.

basis: Items 0-1: Q2 is the seasonal S&M trough (last Q2 fell 11.5%), and Waterdrop's +RMB450m traffic spend bids up the same channels in the same quarter.
against: Segment demand is strong (item 3, short-term medical +15%), and WDH itself rose 10% on its print.

basis: Items 0-2: consensus sits at guide midpoints while the company has printed at or below the bottom of its range two quarters running, the FY delivery target needs a record Q4 on falling orders, and industry loan sizes contradict the guided ASP rise; 6 of 7 prior prints fell 4-5%.
against: 8.5% short interest near 52-week lows, a call-rich skew and an inflecting peer margin (item 3) set up a relief rally if margin hits about 16%.
